title: Exercise 7B · Q11
summary: Solve the quadratic for x, then multiply the two sides for the area.
alt: Exercise 7B · Q11: A campsite in the shape of a rectangle FGHI has sides (3x + 6) m and (x + 1) m, and the length of the diagonal FH is (4x + 1) m. Find the area of the campsite.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: A campsite **FGHI** is a rectangle with sides **FG = (3x + 6) m** and **GH = (x + 1) m**, and diagonal **FH = (4x + 1) m**. In **ΔFGH**, **∠G = 90°**. Find the area of the campsite.

steps.title: Use the right-angled triangle FGH
steps.narration: The diagonal splits the rectangle into right-angled triangles. In **ΔFGH**, **∠G = 90°**, with **FH** the hypotenuse.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{FH^2} &= \role{legA}{FG^2} + \role{legB}{GH^2} \\ \role{hyp}{(4x+1)^2} &= \role{legA}{(3x+6)^2} + \role{legB}{(x+1)^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Form a quadratic equation
steps.narration: Bring every term to one side so it equals zero.\[\begin{aligned}6x^2 - 30x - 36 &= 0 \\ x^2 - 5x - 6 &= 0\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Factorise and solve
steps.narration: Factorise the quadratic, then read off the roots.\[\begin{aligned}(x - 6)(x + 1) &= 0 \\ x = 6 \;&\text{or}\; x = -1\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Choose the valid value
steps.narration: A length can't be negative, so reject **x = −1**.\[\begin{aligned}\therefore x = \role{ans}{6}\quad(\text{since } x > 0)\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Find the sides
steps.narration: Substitute **x = 6** into FG and GH.\[\begin{aligned}FG &= 3(6) + 6 = 24\ \text{m} \\ GH &= 6 + 1 = 7\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Area of the campsite
steps.narration: Multiply the two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\text{Area} &= FG \times GH \\ &= 24 \times 7 = \role{ans}{168\ \text{m}^2}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

challenges.title: Which root?
challenges.prompt: The equation gives x = 6 or x = −1. Which value can x take here?
challenges.explain: A length must be positive, so x = 6. The root x = −1 is rejected.

takeaways: Pythagoras' theorem works only in **right-angled** triangles — mark every right angle in the figure first.
Split the figure into right-angled triangles and solve them **one at a time**; each answer feeds the next triangle.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Don't stop at x
notes.text: The question asks for the **area**, not x — substitute x back into the side expressions first.
